steps.text: Combine broth, rice, celery, onions, water, and bouillon in a large pot over high heat; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until the rice has absorbed most of the liquid, about 30 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat; gradually add flour, stirring continuously to make a thick paste. Whisk in 4 cups of milk, 1/2 cup at a time, whisking constantly, until smooth.

Stir sauce and chopped chicken into rice mixture; add some or all of the remaining 2 cups of milk to reach desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper; simmer over low heat, stirring every 15 minutes, for 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Chicken and Rice Soup
raw_recipe.description: This creamy chicken and rice soup is packed with cooked chicken, brown rice, garlic, and vegetables for a warming, rich and comforting meal.
raw_recipe.name: Creamy Chicken and Rice Soup

review.reviewBody: Hi all! Thanks for trying my recipe. Just a few things that the "recipe' people changed from my original recipe: 1) I always use butter not margarine, 2) I always use roasted garlic flavored chicken broth so if you use regular chicken broth try adding a few cloves of minced garlic, and 3) recently I've substituted 1/4 cup of the liquids with 1/4 cup sherry cooking wine. Of all the recipes I've created, this one is by far my favorite! Take care!

I loved this soup, but must admit I made many changes because I knew what would suit me best. I cooked the chicken, rice and vegetables (mirepoix) separately. In addition to the broth (no water), I added about 3/4 c. of white wine and reduced the liquid to concentrate the flavors. I made the roux separately and added to the reduced liquid, then added 2 c. milk and 1 c. half & half. I added more milk until I got the consistency I wanted. The chicken was cut into chunks (instead of chopped), as I desired larger pieces to bite into. And reduced the amount of rice to only 1 c. cooked. Based on other reviewers, additional seasonings were added: bay leaf, rosemary, thyme, salt and pepper, and fresh parsley at the end. Many changes, but the end result was just what I was looking for. Thank you for the base recipe which allowed me to improvise and adapt it to my liking. I will make it again and again.

Use wild rice for an authentic taste, not brown rice as brown rice will get mushy. And - never use margarine in any recipe at any time - do not even buy it - they should not allow it to be sold. Butter is the healthy way to go - always.

This is such a good comfort food for the 18 degree weather we are experiencing! I read all the reviews, and made the following adjustments: This is for half a recipe. I first sauted then cut up chicken in about 2 T olive oil with some bottled chopped garlic, and seasoned it with salt, pepper, some red pepper flakes, and a shake or two of Creole seasoning I removed the chicken and used the remainling oil to saute about 1 1/2C each chopped onion and carrots ( I use a Mandolin dicer) . I cut the amt. of rice in half, ie.1/2C and here's a hint. Brown rice takes forever to get tender! It took extra liquid to get it soft and fluffy. I used only about 3T of flour in a half stick of butter, and cooked it slowly until it had browned a bit. I thought it made a nice amount of soup, but 4 of us (3 men, 1 woman) cleaned it up!

Made per the recipe, I thought this was a bit bland and tedious (use 2 different pots for 1 pot of soup?), but second time with some tweaking it was delicious. Second time around I sautéed veggies (and added carrots) in HALF of the butter (I subbed butter for margarine), then added broth & cooked rice. I used white rice because that's what I had. When rice was cooked, in a jar I shook together flour & +- 1/2 cup milk & added to the broth mixture. This needs to come to a boil to remove the "floury" flavor. Then added milk to the proper consistency. Both times I used canned chicken, as I have a family member with chewing issues who needs absolutely soft chicken. Added 2 teaspoons of Italian seasoning, and a little more low sodium chicken bullion cubes to add depth of flavor. Second time around it knocked everyone's socks off!

This recipe is a go to in my family. I've been making it for almost 5 years now, and don't plan on stopping anytime soon.
My family like our soup with a bit more substance so my changes were:
- Add carrot (about 1/2 - 1c.) and 1 minced garlic clove
- Saute carrots, garlic, and celery before adding rice and broth.
- Substitue water and chicken bouillon with 1 can of chicken broth (1 3/4 c.)
- Cut brown rice down to a little over 1 c.
- Saute the onion in the butter
- Cut butter down to 1/2 c.
- Cut flour down to 1/3 c.
- Saute chicken in olive oil and season with black pepper, salt, and garlic seasoning.
- Once everything is combined, add poultry seasoning, salt, and pepper.

For best results let this soup sit for longer than an hour, it deffinitly helps enhance the flavor.

This is a great base guideline recipe with tons of room for self expression / your own twists! So I followed most of the recipe…instead of canned broth I used 900ml liquid chicken broth. Recipe calls for 6 cups of milk, I did 3 cups regular 3 cups coconut milk! I of course used chicken both dark and white meat, but I also put some bacon in. Veg wise I used celery, red onion, white button mushrooms, cubed potatoes, fresh chopped garlic, broccoli, and carrots. Seasonings I used garlic powder, Italian seasoning, oregano, dill, bit of seasoning salt for taste, cracked black pepper, and actually a few dashes of maple bacon seasoning (not enough to over power just enough to give a slight smoky taste) haaaands down my best soup. Hubby had 3 bowls, stepdaughter ate a huge bowl! I had put so much into it I DIDNT end up using any rice! I imagine with rice it would have still been great

Excellent, made some changes, by reading thru reviews took advice from others and then added my own items.
Used 1 C rice, and used about twice as much broth as what is called for making it a creamy soup vs it being too thick. I also used 1/4 C sherry and lots of garlic. When I made the Rue, I used the 1/2 C margarine and 4 T flour and 3 C milk. My family all loved it. Thanks for a great soup!
We love this soup! I have been making this soup for years! It is requested at family gatherings! The only change to the recipe….I add carrots!

Good basic recipe. I didn't quite follow the order, but mostly used all the same ingredients. I sauteed garlic, onion, carrots and celery in butter in pan. Removed to bowl. Added whole chicken breasts to pan and cooked in oil. Chopped up. Made the roux in my soup pot, and added crushed rosemary to that. Added 4 cups milk, added chicken and veggies. Cooked until veggies were almost soft. Added one more cup of milk. Added 3/4 cup uncooked white rice (wild would have been better but I didn't have any) and added salt, pepper, pinch of dill and a little extra garlic powder. Simmered for 20 minutes. My family could not stop saying how delicious it was. I know I strayed from the original recipe, but it was my inspiration. :)

What I did differently , i didnt boil the onions with the broth I actually sauteed the onions with a little bit of garlic in real butter. I didn't use any water just replaced it with more broth as someone suggested. I added carrots!
It tastes wonderful! I love this website :-)
It makes a lot!
We really liked it! I halved the recipe and it needed more liquid. I made it in the crockpot and I added peas. I will make it again!

After reading the one and two star reviews, I was ready to improvise. And it still came out too thick. Cut back drastically on the milk/flour portion, cut back by 1/2 on the rice. Add carrots, corn, green beans, garlic, onion, pepper, marjoram, thyme, rosemary and more butter to the otherwise meager portion of celery asked for. Supplement with more chicken broth to thin it out.
Made my with yellow seasoned rice was awesome
Thick tasteless sludge
I used the changed version of this recipe. Soooo yummy

I followed the recipe, exactly, added some chopped cabbage I had on hand, and added these seasonings: celery seed (about a 1/2 tsp, Thyme, (about 1/2 tsp, and one tsp of onion soup mix. Fabulous taste! So hearty too!

I had to make a few tweaks to this recipe to get it to our desired consistency and flavor. I sauteed the onions and celery with a bit of oil and added some chopped garlic after about 4 minutes. I also added some fresh thyme from my garden. I cut back the amount of rice and did not use all of the white sauce either. We don't like our soups too thick and creamy, so I added additional chicken broth to our desired consistency. After these adjustments, it was pretty good. Would be a good soup to make on a cold night.
